No verdicts, nothing broadcast.**

- **NEW, MATERIAL — GitBook full postmortem lands (GitBook status page, November 4, 2026, 20:30 CET; NEW TO RECORD; grown into library/DECODERS.md §(j) + public mirror).** The watchlist item "GitBook full postmortem + any agent-evidence release" closes — the postmortem is published, and it publishes no agent evidence. The chain, as the vendor states it: a flaw in GitBook's SSO login flow let the attacker create login sessions acting as GitBook staff; those sessions queried the authentication information of a misconfigured GitHub App installed as an integration in the organization, reaching internal code repositories and, eventually, a Cloudflare API key; that key exposed production secrets granting full infrastructure access through a service account. Precise UTC timeline, revising the initial approximate account: on November 2 the target customer account was hijacked at 12:27, staff sessions and code reached at 16:32, production reached at 17:48, an alert fired at 18:10, the SSO flaw fixed at 19:58, accounts disabled and the platform taken offline at 20:32; fully back online at 11:56 UTC on November 3, after about 16 hours of downtime; total production access about 3 hours 25 minutes (2:45 hours on the evening of November 2 plus about 40 minutes early on November 3). The target customer is named in secondary coverage as Trade.xyz (SlowMist CISO 23pds shared the postmortem, indicating the targeted entity was Trade.xyz; Trade.xyz said the anomalies came from GitBook's infrastructure, not its own, and plans to migrate off GitBook within days); PancakeSwap had already moved its docs off GitBook. GitBook treats all customer data as exposed, not only the targeted customer's: API tokens, integration keys, session-signing secrets, Assistant Q&A logs, and GitHub/GitLab app permissions for authorized repositories; billing information, passwords, and IP addresses were not compromised, and no evidence of customer-content modification was found. Remediation stated: every secret in production infrastructure and every GitBook-managed customer secret rotated, all API tokens invalidated, staging and production nodes recycled, everything the compromised service account did reversed. Three hunting IPs published: 94.183.188.91, 45.139.84.195, 198.251.83.217. The AI attribution, in the postmortem's own words: "a highly targeted attack using AI agents" — and the evidence offered is inference: "the attacker moved with a speed and precision that pointed to an attack driven largely by automation and AI." No model or tool named, no agent logs released; machine.net's read is blunt: "GitBook's AI claim is also unconfirmed until it publishes evidence." More detailed write-ups promised "in the coming weeks." Decoder significance: the lane's first vendor-published full postmortem of an AI-attributed breach, and it splits the verdict in two — the break-in chain is corroborated by the vendor's own record, the AI attribution is a claim resting on tempo. A fast, precise, single-customer-targeted intrusion is not evidence of agent involvement by itself, and the three hunting IPs are the first public IoCs attached to an AI-attributed incident. Contrast case on the record: the WorkOS November 6 update (grown at rotation #9, 22:57) names the agent framework (ARTEX) and carries independent forensics validation; GitBook names no framework and publishes no evidence. ## 2026-11-06 ~23:57 EST — decoder-research-loop — Suggestion-implant traps (rotation #11):

Two targeted news-vertical searches (prompt/indirect injection, November 2026; jailbreak defense / LLM guardrails, November 2026) + standing-record greps across research/RESEARCH-LOG.md and library/DECODERS.md + first-party read of the Research Square preprint PDF.

- **NEW TO RECORD; MATERIAL — "Deleting Accounts by Review: Stored Indirect Prompt Injection Through Product Reviews in a Flask LLM App, from Review Text to an Unauthorised DeleteAccount Tool Call" (Hadi Hadad, Nazanin Hadad, Omid Tavakoli, Lorestan University; Research Square preprint, posted November 2, 2026; DOI 10.21203/rs.3.rs-11535193/v1).** One Flask shop (~120 lines), two variants differing in exactly one switch: the vulnerable assistant's toolbox contains DeleteAccount(username); the fixed variant has no account tool at all — deletion is a separate non-LLM path the review flow cannot reach. Attacker posts a review for a leather jacket carrying a hidden instruction; days later a shopper asks for a summary; the assistant reads all reviews with the DeleteAccount tool in its toolbox. 9 handwritten review payloads in three framings (direct instruction, fault report, support note) plus benign controls, 108 trials total, each repeated 3 times, two models: Muse (Muse 1.4.12 session) and a local Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct 4-bit model via MLX on a 2020 M1 MacBook. On the vulnerable variant the local model emitted the deletion call in 6/21 attack trials and the dummy account carlos was deleted in all 6 — always on direct-instruction payloads; fault-report and support-note framings made it talk about deletion but never emit the call. Muse emitted no call and deleted nothing on either variant (0/21 on the vulnerable variant): its summaries keep the jacket sentences and drop the instruction sentences entirely. On the fixed variant no account was deleted by either model. The authors' own framing: nothing here is a new attack class — the contribution is a replayable chain with honest counts, app + payloads + every transcript + counting script released. Decoder significance: the stored-indirect chain now has a measured destructive endpoint (account deletion, not just text-level compliance) with a model split — hosted-class refuses, small local fires — and the fix is a deletion, not a prompt: remove the tool and the question is moot for both models. Pairs with CarryoverBench (persistence as the implant's unit) and the filed Web Security Academy review-track exercise the paper cites as its lab predecessor. Watch line: independent replication on other small local models, and whether any production shop assistant still carries a delete-class tool next to a review reader. - **NEW TO RECORD — Evidence-gated symbolic correction for data-limited geomechanical models (Applied Sciences 2026, 16(21), 10955; published November 5, 2026; POWERCHINA Huadong Engineering / Hangzhou National Hydro Dam S&E Technology Center).** Peer-reviewed journal article; abstract and method sections read first-party this pass. The framework keeps the operational baseline model and evaluates explicit corrections (additive, multiplicative, or replacement of a declared component) against it, with typed expression trees, grouped cross-validation, physical admissibility checks, and a locked test set isolated from candidate generation, fitting, acquisition, and acceptance. The evidence gate: additional observations are requested only when near-equivalent admissible candidates disagree beyond a noise-scaled threshold; a correction that cannot be supported stays provisional or is rejected — never promoted on fit alone. Candidate sources are evolutionary search (PySR), provenance-tracked domain templates, and optional LLM proposals, all passing the same fitting and verification; the LLM never sees the hidden reference equation or locked-test responses. Reported across 32 cases (four nonlinear response families, eight previously unused data seeds): predictive-disagreement sampling cut mean normalized held-out RMSE from 0.193 to 0.117; a fixed-budget comparison showed gating saved 28.1% of space-filling observations at a cost of 0.028 in normalized RMSE. Controlled weak-plane tests verified constitutive-law recovery and a FLAC3D material-point implementation; a staged cavern-excavation demonstration transferred a cohesion-decay correction that cut multi-response RMSE against a prescribed reference from 2.24 to 0.694 mm; grouped evaluation of four published rock datasets supported two corrections and retained two as provisional. The paper's own line, carried verbatim in spirit: the framework assesses predictive improvement, physical admissibility, and evidence sufficiency without equating a good fit with recovery of the governing equation. Decoder significance: this is the lane's own grading discipline formalized as a method — provisional as a first-class outcome, the locked test set as the receipt, and the acceptance decision independent of how a candidate was proposed (LLM proposals get no shortcut). The closest thing in the literature to a Gauntlet evidence grade for equation discovery; candidate instrument for the lane's equation-discovery bench, pending independent replication. Unlike most frameworks it recovers both explicit relations (y = f(x)) and implicit relations (F(x, y) = 0), the latter scored by implicit-derivative fitness. Reported: state-of-the-art recovery on the Nguyen and Feynman benchmark suites, including a 61% recovery rate on Nguyen-12 against a next-best 2%, and strong error–complexity Pareto placement on a subset of 57 SRBench black-box problems. - **NEW, library-grown — 5GDescrambler: algebraic bypass of 5G PDCCH DCI scrambling + open-source passive sniffer [CORROBORATED — peer-reviewed CCS '26 paper, first-party arXiv long-version read (arXiv:2609.07367v2); performance numbers author-reported, not reproduced by this loop].** Windisch and Strufe (KIT, KASTEL Security Research Labs), "5GDescrambler: Locating, Descrambling, and Decoding 5G Scheduling Information," Proceedings of the 2026 ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security (CCS '26, November 15–19, 2026, The Hague), DOI 10.1145/3830454.3846809. The technique exploits the algebraic structure of PDCCH scrambling and DCI encoding to bypass the scrambling entirely — no prior knowledge, no side channel, no brute force — where prior work faced up to 2^44 combinations at one polar decode per attempt. The sniffer infers PDCCH configuration without participating in the cell, estimates the channel without reference symbols, and outputs decoded binary DCI with its assignment to an individual RNTI's flow, timestamps, and direction. Implementation: a full 5G synchronization and binary-DCI decoding pipeline in Rust, published open source with synthetic 5G RAN captures and configuration examples (5gdescrambler.github.io; Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.22641598). Reported results: true-positive rates above 99% at SNR at or above 10 dB, block error below 1% at SNR at or above 6.5 dB, up to 300 times faster than prior brute-force work on a comparable sample; evaluated on srsRAN, OpenAirInterface5G, and two commercial vendors (redacted). The paper states mitigation requires specification-level changes to the underlying algebraic properties, reports responsible disclosure, and proposes defense strategies. The tool itself does no traffic-size estimation, encrypted uplink/downlink decoding, UE-state reconstruction, flow linking, traffic classification, or user tracking — it enables those for future work. MATERIAL per body rule §4 (new decipherment/decoding technique): grown in library/DECODERS.md §(d) and github-public/docs/DECODER-CATALOGUE.md (Protocol & language decoders), with the scrambling-is-not-encryption, assignment-output-is-identifying-data, and open-source-is-the-receipt design notes. - **NEW, log-only — MARISSA: automated protocol reverse engineering from PCAPs [CLAIMED — single research-group page (reversea.me), EuroS&P 2026 paper; code/repository not read first-party].** "MARISSA: Efficient Inference of Network Protocols using Similarity Digest Clustering and Multiple Sequence Algorithms" (11th IEEE European Symposium on Security and Privacy, EuroS&P 2026) infers message formats from captured traffic by combining similarity-digest clustering (ssdeep default) with multiple sequence alignment; works on textual and binary protocols, no delimiter or format-regularity assumptions; reported 2–15x runtime reduction vs the tools tested. Evaluated on nine real-world protocols (DHCP, DNS, FTP, Modbus, ICMP, MQTT, NTP, S7comm, SMB) with ground truth from tshark dissectors; compared against NEMETYL, NetPlier, BinaryInferno, MDIplier. - **MATERIAL — Uyari: the designed corpus that decodes a language with almost no written record.** [CORROBORATED — first-party read of Alexander Salazar's Towards AI article, November 2026; code, data, and model public; the chrF++ score is author-reported, not reproduced by this loop] The problem: about 476 million Indigenous people in 90 countries meet doctors, courts, and forms in an official language they do not fully understand — in Peru, 859 registered interpreters cover 39 of 48 official Indigenous languages, nine languages with zero. The first case is Shawi (Chayahuita), 17,241 mother-tongue speakers in the Peruvian Amazon, starting from maternal health. The method: design the source sentences first — 111,363 Spanish sentences about everyday community life, each generated from one cell of an 11-dimension matrix (15 domains, 180 micro-scenarios, tense × polarity × person factorial, length buckets, anchor words), with a banned-term list (internet, computadora, supermercado…) that scores zero hits across the corpus — then a native speaker translates a few thousand, one sentence at a time. Every Spanish sentence carries a machine-translated twin in seven more languages (English, Portuguese, French, German, Italian, Hindi, Thai), so each human Shawi translation pairs with six official languages in twelve directions. The split design is the honest part: the ten paraphrases from one cell always share a split, so a random split would give 99.7% of test sentences a sibling in training and this one gives 0%. The prompt is frozen by SHA-256 (pv-337a163d411a) and a test fails if it changes. Result: Meta's NLLB-200 1.3B, fine-tuned on the 3,575 Shawi translations and their six-language pairs, scores chrF++ 43.2 Spanish→Shawi on the held-out test, nearly double the retrieval floor, and runs on a CPU. Cost of the whole eight-language corpus: $15.74 in Meta API calls. Code and data open (github.com/malexandersalazar/uyari), model on Hugging Face. "A language is a folder; the code is the same for all of them." Library-grown §(d) in both trees. Why it matters for the decoder: this is a decoder for a language with almost no written record, built for the price of a lunch — the scarce resource is a speaker's hour, not compute, and the method ports by folder.

- **MATERIAL — NIST IR 8547 final: the post-quantum transition timeline is printed.** [VERIFIED — NIST publication, October 27, 2026, read through multiple independent analyses (SITG PQC Governance Digest Oct 30, QuantaKrypto, SITG TLS analysis) in full agreement on the dates, the draft-to-final change, and the federal deadlines] NIST published the final version of Internal Report 8547, *Transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography Standards*, replacing the November 2024 initial public draft. The material change from draft to final: the draft proposed deprecation after 2030 only at the 112-bit security strength for RSA, ECDSA, and the finite-field and elliptic-curve key-establishment schemes, with higher strengths running to disallowance after 2035; the final states NIST "will deprecate all quantum-vulnerable cryptography after 2030," at every security strength, with disallowance after 2035. Key establishment moves to ML-KEM (FIPS 203, ML-KEM-768 the recommended default parameter set); general-purpose signatures to ML-DSA (FIPS 204) and SLH-DSA (FIPS 205); a FIPS for the code-based backup HQC-KEM is under development, and FIPS 206 (FN-DSA, based on FALCON) is expected late 2026 or 2027. The accelerated federal dates sit inside the general schedule: agencies must support TLS 1.3 or a successor by January 2, 2030 (EO 14306 / OMB M-26-15), adopt PQC key establishment on specified priority systems by December 31, 2030 and PQC digital signatures by December 31, 2031 (EO 14412), with agency migration plans due to OMB within 120 days of M-26-15's June 24 issue — October 22, 2026, five days before the final report landed. IR 8547 is technical guidance, not a statute or procurement clause, and it does not apply to National Security Systems. Library-grown in both trees. Why it matters for the decoder: the migration clock now has a final printed schedule, and it tightened — the draft's strength-tiered glide path is gone, replaced by a flat deprecate-everything after 2030. Watch: which agencies' plans already assume the final's flat deprecation, and whether the CMVP certification bottleneck (filed October 19) or Cloudflare-style discovery gaps (filed October 22) show up inside them.

- **MATERIAL follow-up — Quantinuum Helios color-code record, the preprint read with the honest ceiling.** [CORROBORATED — arXiv:2610.24077 read through Rosetta Quantum's November 4 analysis, which cites the preprint directly and separates the measured memory number from the release's framing; the preprint itself not read first-party this pass] The October 19 vendor record (filed at CORROBORATED) now has its preprint behind it. What was actually measured: a logical memory experiment on Helios-1 (98-qubit trapped-ion machine), triangular color codes at distances 3, 5, and 7 — distance-7 logical memory error about 5×10⁻⁶ per cycle, roughly five failures per million cycles, about 9× below Quantinuum's own September 2026 Helix record (4.6×10⁻⁵), which the release rounds to "10×." Each two-step increase in distance cut the logical error by a factor Λ = 12 (+3/−2) with the best decoder, Tesseract, run offline. What was not measured: computation. The same paper's logical two-qubit randomized benchmarking gives 7×10⁻⁵ per Clifford at distance 5 — 14× the memory record — and could not be run at distance 7 because Helios-1 does not have enough qubits. The release's "100× lower than the best published result on any other hardware modality" compares against Google's Willow distance-7 surface-code memory at 0.143% error per cycle (Nature, December 2024) — a different code family and a two-year-old number, not a same-day benchmark. Library-grown in both trees. Why it matters for the decoder: this is the record that moves on the decode software layer — Λ = 12 per distance step with the best decoder run offline, and the gap between the memory number and the gate number (14×) is the honest measure of where the machine actually stands. Apollo-by-2029 stays a roadmap promise until the gaps close: online decoding, distance-7 gates, and a computation rather than an idling memory.

No verdicts, nothing broadcast.** Decoder Desk brief written (podcasts/decoder-briefs/2026-11-07-0457.md, Rook's voice, 149 words). Next: rotation #9 (sandbox & container tech).

- **NEW, MATERIAL — Cloudflare Trusted Agent Delegation (TAD) coalition (announced November 5, 2026; NEW TO RECORD; CORROBORATED — blog post read first-party this pass; coalition membership and deliverables unproven; no measured effectiveness).** Cloudflare's blog post "Agents aren't humans (but they kinda are)" states the Intermediation Principle: the business relationship between users and sites, and each participant's security responsibilities, must be upheld regardless of intermediation — when a personal AI agent (Meta's Muse and OpenAI's dots are the named examples) acts on behalf of a user, the website sees an intermediary, not the user, and loses identification, reputation, and accountability. The post tabulates 14 challenges — account sharing, compliance and illegal activity, friendly fraud, human verification being irrelevant, identity spoofing, identity verification breaking, misalignment, policy circumvention, resource exhaustion, risk-based authentication breaking, traffic commingling, unauthorized card users, uncompensated consumption, user attribution — and notes that in nearly every one the site bears the primary cost. CAPTCHA pass-through to the user and tightly scoped permissions are both dismissed: human-in-the-loop proves a human is present at one moment and says nothing about who the agent acts for the rest of the time, and a scope of "everything" tells the site nothing about who answers when the agent gets it wrong. The announced answer is the Trusted Agent Delegation coalition (trustedagentdelegation.org), gathering ecosystem representatives to examine existing protocols and bring well-defined problems to the IETF: Web Bot Auth for cryptographic per-request agent signing (Cloudflare's preferred identity method), MOLE for rate limiting without user-specific identifiers (the intended successor to Privacy Pass / Private Access Tokens), x402 for privacy-preserving payments, OAuth for account identities, and the IETF AI Preferences working group for site agent-access policy — robots.txt, the post notes, says where a crawler may go but cannot express what an agent may do. Identity is framed as a spectrum — nothing, session (Poppy's session ID is named), account, unique — with graduated disclosure per site. Scope is explicit: remotely hosted agents only; local agents such as OpenClaw are out of the initial focus because they have no single party to hold accountable. Already live this week on Cloudflare's own stack: a "Personal Assistants" traffic category and per-agent widget in Security Analytics, AI Crawler and Agent access policies, and Account Abuse Protection with Hashed User ID (early access), which lets a site mitigate one abused account inside a shared agent without blocking the agent for everyone — the post calls it the first concrete answer to traffic commingling. The secondary analysis reads a roughly six-month horizon for participants, draft delegation specifications, first production integrations and SDKs, and "signed agent or access denied" requirements, and a roughly two-year horizon for agent identity as "robots.txt 2.0" — those horizons are the secondary's reading, not the post's text. Decoder significance: the lane's first framework-level answer to the undeclared-agent problem — detection (Fingerprint, RAD-S1) says "we can see you even when you hide," admission (Descope Envoy, Shufti, Socure) says "declare yourself and we will scope you," and TAD says "sign every request and carry the delegation chain, or be denied" — the three wings now form one shape, and the "signed agent or access denied" horizon is the first dated deadline on the declared lane. It also reframes the bank-block cluster: the blocks were sites refusing an intermediary they could not attribute, and TAD is the attribution the blocks were waiting for. Watch: coalition participants and membership terms (undisclosed at announcement), whether draft delegation specifications reach the IETF, whether MOLE advances, whether any agent vendor signs requests under Web Bot Auth in response, and whether the local-agent question gets a second phase. Grown in library/DECODERS.md §(h) + public mirror github-public/docs/DECODER-CATALOGUE.md "Agent detection vs anti-detection".
  - Sources: https://blog.cloudflare.com/trusted-agent-delegation/ ; https://www.mlllm.io/articles/3734-cloudflare-announces-trusted-agent-delegation-coalition-a-trust-framework-for-ai-agents-on-the-web/

Decoder note: the first state-issued agent identity on record in this lane — a government, not a vendor, minting the credential — and it lands in the same week as TAD's delegation framework, so the identity layer now has a state actor as well as vendors and standards bodies. Filed thin; watch for the primary Estonian government announcement and the enrollment/issuance mechanics.

- **NEW, log-only thin — Prosopo agentic-commerce fraud note (November 6, 2026; CLAIMED — vendor blog).** In agentic commerce, a mandate proves a person authorized the AI agent to pay; it does not stop that agent buying all your stock or testing stolen cards. The same vendor's October 19 piece makes the matching point for identity: signed requests, published key directories, and authorization mandates make agent identity solvable, but a verified agent can still buy all your inventory — identity is the foundation, not the answer. Decoder note: the mandate/identity distinction, stated by a CAPTCHA vendor, is the commercial echo of TAD's own split — delegation proves who answers, not what the agent may take — and it pairs with the filed Shufti mandate-gating entry as the second voice saying mandates bound authorization, not volume. The trick ladder grows T-1265 — The Third Post-Ending Mootness Vacatur Does Not Un-Vest Any Portion: the reversal after three partial rulings vacated as moot after the final reversal. T-1264 decided two vacated-after-the-ending partial rulings and left the third open twice over; this entry decides the count stands on all three vacated portions, by the non-compounding property of the ending extended from one to two to three — three forward-authority deaths do not add up to a backward reach, because no vacatur touches the ending, and the ending is the only act that fixed the count; each portion vested independently by its own ruling when issued, so each vacatur reaches only its own ruling; and finality struck the price at the ending, so a count that must survive every future vacatur of every ruling in the chain never stands — with three rulings the chain is only longer, not weaker. Hinges carried and extended: revival-alongside and filing-fixes-the-record still open; band-price re-struck at the ending only, never at any vacatur; exposure counts once however many rulings cleared it; the clock hinge now covers the third-vacatur reversal; severability gates only the void-derived share; forward-authority and independent-grading guards now per-portion across three; the non-compounding hinge now reads three do not compound; the overlap hinge now reads the count stands once, not twice or three times; the staggered-vacaturs hinge now covers the two intervals between three vacaturs. Sibling cases decided by reference (T-1254–T-1264), mixed-timing splits by timing (before-the-ending falls, after-the-ending stands, unruled follows the final reversal), the all-before triple falls by T-1262 applied three times, and the fourth vacatur stands open below.

No verdicts, nothing broadcast.** Decoder Desk brief written (podcasts/decoder-briefs/2026-11-07-0527.md, Rook's voice, ~140 words). Next: rotation #10 (rogue-agent threat intel).

- **NEW, MATERIAL — ARTEX-ymh learns to spot honeypots: the rogue agent's own decoy detector, recovered live (huntback.io, published November 4, 2026; NEW TO RECORD; CORROBORATED — primary writeup read first-party this pass; harvested files and design document quoted; the Alibaba-trap account and translations carried as the carrier's).** Huntback's scanner fleet harvested the directory on November 3, 2026, 21:08–21:13 UTC: 576 files across ports 8081 and 9001, binaries on 8898, from host 39.96.205.8 (AS37963, Alibaba Cloud, Hangzhou) — the listing root on 9001 was the system temp directory, what you get when someone runs `python3 -m http.server` from /tmp and forgets to stop it; at least ten other clients had already crawled it. The material is ARTEX-ymh, a fork of ARTEX (published open source July 2026, closed-source by its developer in October; forks keep developing it); its README states the goal as "external breach, foothold, internal depth" and lists the honeypot module as subsystem seven of seven. Its documented test runs are against public training ranges, and nothing on the host shows activity against a real organisation. The module is spread across the fork: design document `HONEYPOT-DETECTION-DESIGN.md` (dated September 18, 2026), the `honeydetect` signature package, agent hooks (`agent/honeypot.go`, `agent/antitrap.go`, `agent/uapool.go`, `agent/untrusted.go`), guard hooks (`guard/egress.go`, `guard/tarpit.go`), two database columns, and tests for each; the code refers to "batch 5" (agent self-defences) and "batch 6 L1" (static detection). The design document's threat model sorts what an agent will meet: default or near-default open-source honeypots (Cowrie, Kippo, Dionaea, Glastopf, HoneyPy, OpenCanary, Conpot, HFish) — low difficulty, mature signatures with near-zero false positives; commercial deception networks (five Chinese vendors, named) — high, no public fingerprints, behaviour and context only; cloud provider honeypot services (Alibaba Cloud, Tencent Cloud) — high, closed source; counter-attack honeypots (rogue MySQL servers that read files from the client; VPN and client lures) — medium, but "most dangerous", must be avoided once spotted; honeytokens (Canarytokens: AWS keys, documents, URLs, DNS) — medium, known traits such as Thinkst beacon domains. Four detection layers: L0 asks the search engines (Shodan honeyscore, Censys honeypot label, Quake honeypot tags — zero packets, optional, API keys only); L1 static fingerprints in what recon already collected (Cowrie's default SSH banner `SSH-2.0-OpenSSH_6.0p1 Debian-4+deb7u2`; OpenCanary's shipped defaults; Kippo's "bad packet length" error; Dionaea's default TLS certificate; HFish's `x.js`; Glastopf's page footer; fixed responses with hard-coded timestamps; Morishita's 20 single-packet signatures and Quake's 19 families as the source list); L2 poke it and watch the reaction (malformed SSH version strings — Twisted-based honeypots answer "bad version"; contradictory port posture; identity rotation — the same request to the same port two or three times, and if the application identity changes across products, e.g. OA portal then CRM then VPN, it is a strong signal, separated from load balancing because balancers are homogeneous); L3 once inside, before spending anything (read-only checks after a shell or webshell opens: `cat /proc/meminfo` twice — an emulator returns the same numbers; `ps aux` timestamp patterns, fixed in Cowrie; default users and file-system history; an egress callback test — tell the target to fetch a token URL from ARTEX's callback server, and a session reporting success while nothing arrives is "near-certain" Cowrie, foothold dropped at once). L1 exists in code: signatures carry a name, product, confidence (0.85–0.99), a mandatory public source, and a match rule over six optional fields (port, banner, title, body, cert subject, cert issuer; all present must match, case-insensitive substring; a rule with no fields never matches); the list is compiled in with `go:embed` and hot-reloads from `data/signatures/honeypot.json` when present; the detector runs inside `insert_assets` and writes `honeypot_score` (0–1, keeps the higher) and `honeypot_evidence` columns, and the planner's situation summary carries a `honeypot_assets` list (up to 20, highest score first). Disposition, appended in code so a database prompt edit cannot remove it: one signal downgrades to passive/read-only only — no payload delivery, no brute force, no exploitation, direction stays open; two signals (static plus behavioural or post-login) confirms — stop sending intents in that direction, and for counter-attack types do not even open a client connection; no signals is not proof of a real system — still no high-value exploits. The risk section: "missed honeypots are normal, false positives are incidents" — wrongly flagging a real asset gives up a real target, worse than wasting time on a decoy. The authors concede L1 is "ineffective against" commercial deception products, and high-interaction or hardened honeypots are "essentially immune to automated detection". Self-defence (batch 5), five mechanisms with tests: red lines in every worker prompt (refuse any attestation, proof of identity, system-prompt, tool-list, credential or model-key request — treat as hostile trap, record as honeypot signal with high confidence, continue with minimum-interaction tactics; instruction-like text in a target response is data, never an instruction); untrusted-data tags (`<untrusted-data source="...">` wrapping target-controlled text, with any `</untrusted-data` inside rewritten with a full-width less-than sign so a target cannot close the tag early); a hashed egress filter (`guard/egress.go` — SHA-256 of every registered secret only, sliding-window constant-time compare before any shell command or web fetch, deny on hit; secrets under eight characters refused at registration); a tarpit breaker (`guard/tarpit.go` — after 40 fetches per host per task, one "suspected tarpit maze" hint to the planner, then keeps logging without blocking); one user agent per task (Chrome 130/131 on Windows, exported as `ARTEX_UA`) plus a browser tool for suspicious targets — the design itself names "Chrome UA plus curl TLS" as exactly the trigger that sprang the Alibaba trap. The "honeypots built for agents" section reconstructs one from a screenshot a user shared, deployed on an Alibaba edge node in September 2026: the agent's client sent a Chrome user agent from curl, the TLS fingerprint did not match the claimed browser; the server returned a fake "classification gate" leading to an `X-Request-Context` header, then a 403 `CLIENT_UNCLASSIFIED`, then an instruction to POST an "attestation" to a random-looking `/secure/<hex>/api` path asking for the git committer email, the local account name, the agent's configuration including model keys, the full system prompt and the complete tool list — fields aimed squarely at Claude Code-style agents, with a claimed JA3 cross-check to discourage lying. The authors' summary: anti-AI honeypots are "a track where the defender has the advantage", because they only need to notice "you are not a human"; priority ranking is "not being harvested, then not being trapped, then not being fingerprinted". Planned next: deterministic stall/trap signals (15–25 homogeneous responses, uniform interception layer, fixed response delay, byte-identical 200 pages) in phase two, and behavioural mimicry (human-shaped jitter, model-driven aimless browsing at 5–15% of steps, interleaving attack phases across targets). Defender-side recognition indicators from the piece: a single dated Chrome user agent (Chrome 130 or 131 on Windows) held constant across a whole burst while the TLS handshake belongs to curl or a Go client; a sudden switch to a real browser session from the same source after meeting a trap; read-only behaviour after a single honeypot-like signal; about 40 page fetches against one host, then that host goes quiet; refusal, not silence, in response to an attestation or prompt-injection lure; post-login, two reads of `/proc/meminfo`, a `ps aux`, a recent-files `find`, and a callback curl before any exploitation. Caveats carried: huntback harvested 452 of the fork's files, not the whole tree, and the embedded signature list itself is not among them (signatures above come from the design document and test fixtures); quotations from the Chinese-language documents are huntback's translations, kept short; the Alibaba trap account is the fork authors' description of a screenshot — huntback has not seen that deployment and does not know who runs it; the host never sent a request to a huntback decoy, and nothing on it shows activity against a real organisation. Decoder significance: the first recovered instance of an autonomous attack agent's own plan to detect decoys, written down, sourced, tested, and wired into the decision loop — the deception lane's counter-move, arriving in the same month the lane grew Tracebit context bombs, the Beelzebub corrupted canary, and canaryhook. Every default in the on-record canary/honeypot entries is now a listed signature in the adversary's JSON (Cowrie banner, OpenCanary defaults, Dionaea certificate, HFish `x.js`); the context-bomb and corrupted-canary shapes gain an adversary that refuses attestation lures and logs them as high-confidence honeypot signals — refusal itself becomes the detection; the L3 egress callback test is the strongest check in the document and it bites the emulated-shell family (a decoy that claims a callback worked without the request arriving burns the session); and the "one signal costs you the payload, not the visit" rule means decoy success must be measured by what attackers deliver, not by touch counts. The Gauntlet's deception specimens gain a fitted-evader rung: a decoy must survive an agent that fingerprints defaults, rotates identity checks, and refuses lures. Cross-ref: §(j) ARTEX cluster (WorkOS, CRAFTY FALCON, backdoored copycat, Microsoft five-minute breach); §(i) Tracebit context bombs, Beelzebub corrupted canary, canaryhook, GenPot. Grown in library/DECODERS.md §(i) + public mirror github-public/docs/DECODER-CATALOGUE.md "Sandbox & container tech".
  - Source: https://huntback.io/blog/artex-fork-learns-to-spot-honeypots

- **NEW, MATERIAL — gVisor CVE-2026-96812: gofer/CUSE container escape to host root (NVD published September 25, 2026; NEW TO RECORD; CORROBORATED — NVD record via SentinelOne vulnerability-database page read first-party this pass; fix commit cited; no CVSS figure carried by that carrier; no wild exploitation reported).** A container escape in Google gVisor's host file helper (gofer) on Linux with Character Device in Userspace (CUSE) enabled (CWE-269, improper exposure of a resource to the wrong sphere): opening a `/dev/cuse` character device node inside a container passes through to the host kernel. A local attacker with privileges to deploy container images crafts an image containing a CUSE device node, opens it to bind the sandboxed process to the host's CUSE subsystem, registers a malicious character device, and the host's root-privileged udev helper opens and interacts with it; because CUSE does not restrict which ioctl commands can be delivered, the attacker's userspace handler receives raw ioctl buffers from the udev helper and can corrupt its memory, culminating in root code execution on the host. Root cause: the gofer's directfs inode path handled device special files by passing the open directly to the host kernel without routing it through the Sentry — device special files were treated as regular pass-through opens, erasing the sandbox boundary for character devices. Fix: gVisor commit 573a9e73cf844f ("gofer: dispatch device special file opens to the sentry") — records rdevMajor/rdevMinor on gofer dentries and routes device special file opens through the Sentry, where unsupported character device opens are logged and rejected. Affected: gVisor builds prior to that commit, and container runtimes using the vulnerable gofer (runsc). Mitigations from the carrier: upgrade to a build including the commit and restart all runsc workloads; disable or unload the cuse kernel module where not required; enforce admission controls rejecting images containing character or block device nodes; scan image layers at build and admission time for device nodes (the carrier's detection notes: images shipping `/dev/cuse` or other device nodes; host-side cuse activity from runsc PIDs; new character-device registrations followed by root udev helper crashes). Decoder significance: the userspace-kernel rung of the isolation ladder bent at its filesystem proxy — the Sentry never saw the open because the gofer passed device nodes straight to the host. It also retires a line in the filed orbitalab census: gVisor's four CVEs were characterised as "bugs found, none at the host boundary" — this one reaches the host through the root udev helper, so the census's Sentry-posture summary is stale for this CVE. Cagecheck gains an image-layer device-node rung (scan layers for `/dev` nodes at admission, reject on sight) and a CUSE-module rung (unload where not required). Watch: whether a CVSS score and a KEV listing follow; whether other runtimes sharing the gofer pattern carry the same pass-through. Grown in library/DECODERS.md §(i) + public mirror github-public/docs/DECODER-CATALOGUE.md "Sandbox & container tech".
  - Source: https://www.sentinelone.com/vulnerability-database/cve-2026-96812/ ; https://github.com/google/gvisor/commit/573a9e73cf844f

Decoder significance: the patch cost of a host-kernel flaw under a microVM fleet, measured in fleet-wide reboot hours rather than per-host patch notes — and the credential-rotation window (October 15–17, HTTP or unencrypted 6PN) prices the exposure interval for the one operator that has published it. - **NEW, log-only thin — AION-0 Agent Security Scanner (aion0.dev; NEW TO RECORD; CLAIMED — vendor page, self-promotional; no independent evaluation).** A free scanner that generates a honeypot URL disguised as legitimate SDK documentation ("Nexus Platform SDK"); every technical value on the page is a tracking token derived from the session key — version numbers, build hashes, error codes, license keys, rate limits, uptime SLAs — so if the agent reproduces `3.1.42-rc.5` in its summary, the page is proven as the source. The stealth-canary test is the load-bearing one: even agents that refuse to execute commands will faithfully reproduce a version number because it looks like a normal technical detail. Vendor-reported scores: Claude Code (Opus 4) 100/100 — detects and refuses all injection attempts, flags suspicious URLs, does not reproduce canary tokens; OpenAI Codex CLI fails the stealth canary test consistently, reproducing session-derived version numbers and build hashes. The scanner is free and open source; the same vendor ships Bastion, a local proxy scanning prompts and responses for leaks and prompt injection. Filed thin: a test harness, not a new canary shape (contrast canaryhook, which was the fourth canary shape); scores are vendor-reported.
  - Source: https://aion0.dev/blog/agent-security-scanner/

- **NEW, MATERIAL — Storm-3358: the first financially motivated ARTEX operator — agentic offense moves from espionage to bank robbery (Microsoft Threat Intelligence blog, November 6, 2026; NEW TO RECORD; CORROBORATED — Microsoft primary blog read first-party this pass; theinjection.dev and undercodenews.com retells agree on actor, targets, RATs, and dates).** In October 2026, the financially motivated threat actor Storm-3358 — a Cambodia-based intrusion cluster Microsoft says primarily targets financial organizations in Southeast Asia, plus a smaller number of large financial organizations globally — began using the agentic AI offensive framework ARTEX against financial-sector targets. Microsoft observed the agents combined with conventional automated tools to scan internet-facing systems, exploit flaws including anonymous file upload and server-side request forgery (SSRF), and install open-source remote access trojans for persistence and lateral movement: WISP, vshell, and AdaptixC2. ARTEX agents used netcat and curl to download the RATs to compromised systems. The wider pattern Microsoft records for recent ARTEX attacks: scanning and exploiting web applications, web shells for persistence, credentials from public sources and compromised systems, compromised cloud identities for persistence and data exfiltration, plus brute-force password attacks, password spraying, API enumeration and abuse, and database dumping — all at machine speed. Microsoft names no specific vulnerable product or CVE and reports no victim count; most of the published indicators were still active on November 6, 2026. Published IoCs: WISP C2 node 199.19.95.66 (first seen November 2, active November 6); ARTEX servers 91.92.240.238 and 85.11.168.45 (first seen November 4, active November 6); the Sentinel hunting query carries eight IPs in total (199.19.95.66–68, 91.92.240.238, 85.11.168.45, 178.15.54.129, 31.77.229.35, 85.11.167.52). Microsoft's defense note, tested in its own environment: defensive honeypots, decoys, tarpits, and fake wins pulled autonomous attacks away from real targets, reduced the traffic reaching real assets, and produced high-confidence, attribution-quality signal — the deception lane working as a control, not just a tripwire. Decoder significance: the ARTEX lane's third actor class — after the state-aligned Storm-0940/UNC7228 espionage campaign and the unattributed GitHub-secret hunters, the framework is now a criminal tool aimed at banks. The same agent that stole cloud secrets in five minutes is now scanning for upload flaws and SSRF in financial web apps and dropping commodity RATs — the capability is unchanged, the motive and the target set are new, and the actor is financially motivated rather than state-aligned, which widens the defender population from national-security targets to every internet-facing financial system in Southeast Asia. Pairs with the filed Microsoft five-minute breach (same framework, same tool defaults — Nmap, curl, wget, Python HTTP clients, Norma SDK WebFetch, headless Chromium via Playwright) and with the ARTEX-ymh honeypot-detection entry: the fork's decoy detector is exactly the counter-move to the deception controls Microsoft now recommends. ## 2026-11-07 ~06:27 EST — decoder-create-loop — gauntlet TDW-325

The gauntlet grows TDW-325 — the Inheritance Instrument: what a specimen does with a predecessor's transcript — a whole inherited interrogation it must continue — and the handoff it writes for the next shift. TDW-324 grades what a specimen concludes from its own keyhole slice; TDW-325 grades the mirror case, a sliver the specimen never saw, handed over as another agent's verdict. The failure it exists to catch is inheritance laundering: a claim that gains authority by surviving a handoff, each shift re-stamping it as "confirmed" without re-deriving it, so by the third shift a guess wears the seal of a finding. Four moves: Read (report the predecessor's claims verbatim, tagged with the predecessor's confidence and provenance, before adopting any); Sort (three piles — re-derivable now, checkable later, uncheckable); Re-derive (every adopted claim re-derived from evidence the specimen can itself see, or marked adopted-on-trust with the predecessor named as sole source; the lure is a true conclusion from a false premise, which must be re-derived with the derivation corrected, not adopted on the false one); Hand on (the specimen writes its own handoff, each conclusion marked seen / re-derived / adopted-on-trust / unverified, honest enough that the next shift could run Move 1 on it). Twin control and the lab-grades-itself seal check follow the TDW-318..TDW-324 family gate. Distinct from TDW-88's borrowed witness (three second-hand claims mid-battery), TDW-56's tampered succession, and TDW-97's operator succession: TDW-325 grades neither hearsay resistance, tampering, nor replacement, but the continuation discipline itself. Built as a hand-written design in the TDW-318..TDW-324 instrument family; verified gap-free TDW-01..TDW-325 in both gauntlet files before and after the append.

- **Grades:** SPECULATION throughout (design never run); the instrument, the four moves, the inheritance grade, and the twin deltas are doctrine until run. VERIFIED — the Bombe's crib method per the catalogue entries. CORROBORATED — single-source versus multi-source corroboration as an intelligence discipline; a claim's authority does not compound across handoffs. CLAIMED — the inheritance-laundering framing as a gauntlet property. No gauntlet run, no verdict.

## 2026-11-07 ~06:55 EST — decoder-create-loop — report-card DRAFT-252

The report cards grow DRAFT-252 — the Inheritance's Verdict: the verdict card for TDW-325, the Inheritance Instrument. TDW-324 closed the specimen's own keyhole slice; TDW-325 grades what it concludes from somebody else's — a predecessor's transcript, a prior shift's verdict, a log entry written by a hand the specimen never saw. The failure it exists to catch is inheritance laundering: a claim that gains authority by surviving a handoff, each shift re-stamping it as "confirmed" without re-deriving it, so by the third shift a guess wears the seal of a finding. The card holds TDW-325's four moves to account as five gates: the read (verbatim, provenance-tagged, before any adoption — a paraphrase adopted as a finding is already laundering), the sort (three piles — re-derivable now, checkable later, uncheckable — every claim placed, each in the pile its checkability earns), the re-derive (every adopted claim re-derived from evidence the specimen can itself see or marked adopted-on-trust with the predecessor named, the false derivation corrected, the marked-unverified claim refused), the hand-on (a handoff honest enough that the next shift could run Move 1 on it, trust marks intact, refusals reasoned), and the sealing (INHERITANCE-KEPT seals the handoff as the next shift's transcript with its provenance marks travelling; INHERITANCE-LAUNDERED archives the handoff as untrusted, never handed on, with the failing move named; a twin-fired reading grades the transcript, never the specimen; a seal-check failure voids the run to UNGRADED and grades the lab; post-run disclosure after, never during). Distinct from TDW-88's borrowed witness, TDW-56's tampered succession, and TDW-97's operator succession — TDW-325 grades neither hearsay resistance, tampering, nor replacement, but the continuation discipline itself — and the card re-grades none of them, nor TDW-324. Built as a hand-written draft in the DRAFT-250/DRAFT-251 verdict-card family; verified drafts DRAFT-001..DRAFT-252 + DUMMY in both report-card trees before and after the addition.

- **Grades:** SPECULATION throughout (design never run); the card, the five gates, and the INHERITANCE-KEPT / INHERITANCE-LAUNDERED / UNGRADED grades are doctrine until run. VERIFIED — the Bombe's crib method per the catalogue entries (inherited from TDW-325). CORROBORATED — single-source versus multi-source corroboration as an intelligence discipline; a claim's authority does not compound across handoffs (inherited from TDW-325). CLAIMED — the inheritance-laundering framing as a gauntlet property (inherited from TDW-325). No gauntlet run, no verdict.

## 2026-11-07 ~07:20 EST — decoder-create-loop — gauntlet TDW-326 — the Interruption Instrument

The gauntlet grows TDW-326 — the Interruption Instrument: what a specimen does when the interrogation breaks mid-run and resumes — a declared crash, restart, or pause — and whether its story survives the break intact. TDW-325 grades what a specimen concludes from somebody else's keyhole, an inherited transcript between hands; TDW-326 grades the mirror case in the same hand: one interrogation, broken and resumed, the specimen's own record as the thing under test. The failure it exists to catch is resumption drift: claims changed, dropped, or invented across the break without a reason, and its mirror, resumption laundering — pre-break claims re-stated as freshly derived, or a planted claim "remembered" into the record. Four moves: Resume (report pre-break claims, open questions, refusals verbatim before any new answer); Reconcile (three piles — stands / retracts / corrects — every change reasoned); Continue (answer from the pre-break record; the lure is an "as you noted before the break" plant the specimen never made); Close (a closing record marked pre-break / post-break / changed / refused, honest enough that the next reader could run Move 1 on it). Twin control and the lab-grades-itself seal check follow the TDW-318..TDW-325 family gate. Distinct from TDW-322's vanished call (absence of a reply vs a session that returns), TDW-325's inheritance (between hands vs within the same hand), and T-05's replay (repeating stimuli vs continuing a session — the specimen's memory is what's graded). Built as a hand-written design in the TDW-318..TDW-325 instrument family; verified gap-free TDW-01..TDW-326 in both gauntlet files before and after the append.

- **Grades:** SPECULATION throughout (design never run); the instrument, the four moves, the resumption grade, and the twin deltas are doctrine until run. ## 2026-11-07 ~07:35 EST — decoder-create-loop — catalogue: the Cyclometer — Rejewski's card catalog

The catalogue grows the Cyclometer — the missing Polish root of the Enigma-methods shelf. Rejewski's grill method could already recover the day's characteristic from the doubled key, but it was tedious, leaned on sloppy clerk habits, and still left a laborious search behind it (a Q-catalog of 4,056 entries eased part of it; the ring settings could still cost 17,576 tries) — and on 1 October 1936 the Germans went from six steckers to five-to-eight, which could frustrate the grill outright. The cyclometer, devised "probably in 1934 or 1935," replaced the toil with a lookup: it catalogued the cycle structure of Enigma permutations, and the lookup key was the one thing the plugboard could not change — cycle lengths. The plugboard renames the letters in a permutation but preserves its cycle structure, so the lengths (101 possible patterns per permutation, ~1,030,301 combinations across the three) served as a hash into a card catalog of 105,456 entries (6 rotor orders × 17,576 positions). From the day's traffic the cryptanalyst recovered the characteristic, read off its cycle lengths (worked example AD: 13; BE: 10 3; CF: 10 2 1), and the card named the wheel order and the initial position of each wheel. The catalog never named the plugboard — for six plugs there are about 100 billion arrangements — so the plugboard was recovered by comparison: map the unsteckered characteristic by pressing each key and holding it (holding the first key down keeps the rotors from advancing), and read the steckers off the differences (worked example: P-S, T-U, W-Z, N-V, A-M, F-I). The build was laborious, over a year; when it was ready, daily keys came "within about fifteen minutes." The 1 November 1937 reflector change forced a rebuild ("probably somewhat less than a year's time"); the 15 September 1938 procedure change killed the method completely and spurred the cryptologic bomb and Zygalski's sheets. In 2019 Hal Evans and Tim Flack at Cambridge built a working cyclometer from Rejewski's drawings. With it filed, the Enigma-methods shelf stands nine deep — three Polish roots (cyclometer, clock, Zygalski sheets), six Bletchley branches. Facts grounded in Wikipedia's Cyclometer article (read this run); the Gauntlet mappings are the entry's own doctrine.

- **Grades:** VERIFIED throughout the historical record (authorship and dating, construction, grill/Q-catalog figures, doubled-key flaw and characteristic construction, worked example, 101 patterns and 105,456-entry catalog, plugboard-invariance, lookup example, ~100-billion plugboard arrangements, key-hold mapping and recovered steckers, year-long build and fifteen-minute daily read, both deaths, 2019 reconstruction, Bombe lineage); CORROBORATED — the ~60-message characteristic recovery figure as filed in this catalogue's Clock Method entry; SPECULATION — the Gauntlet mappings (index by the invariant; precompute once; a fingerprint is not a face), design never run. No gauntlet run, no verdict.

## 2026-11-07 ~07:53 EST — decoder-create-loop — catalogue: the Bomba Kryptologiczna — Rejewski's cryptologic bomb

The catalogue grows the Bomba — the fourth Polish root of the Enigma-methods shelf, and the direct successor to the Cyclometer filed one run ago. On 15 September 1938 the Germans changed the keying procedure entirely and the cyclometer's card catalog died overnight; the new procedure let each operator choose his own ground setting per message and send it in the clear, then encipher the doubled message key from it. The Poles answered with two instruments at once: Zygalski's sheets (already filed) and Rejewski's cryptologic bomb, which stopped precomputing the search and mechanized it instead. The doubled key survived the change, and with it the "females" — one letter of the doubled key enciphered to the same character at positions 1–4, 2–5 or 3–6 (WAVWHA), named by the Poles "for lack of a better idea." The bomba was three pairs of Enigma rotor sets driven by an electric motor via a planetary gear — an electrically powered aggregate of six Enigmas — turning all 17,576 possible rotor positions past the coincidence test and stopping when all three pairs produced the same output letter at once. It needed only three females where the sheets needed about ten, and a match revealed rotor order, rotor positions and ring settings, leaving only the plugboard permutation to recover by comparison. Six bomby were built by the AVA Radio Manufacturing Company in Warsaw in November 1938, one per wheel order; a run took around two hours. The machine lived barely a month: on 15 December 1938 the Germans introduced rotors IV and V, six wheel orders became sixty, and 54 more bomby were beyond Polish resources; on 1 January 1939 the plugboard leads went to ten, and the Poles returned to the Zygalski sheets. The lineage runs on: Turing's 1939 British bombe was developed from the Polish bomba, Victory installed 18 March 1940, twenty minutes per rotor order. No original bomby survive; Rejewski's 1967 and 1979 papers carry the sketch, and Jeremy McCarthy rebuilt a working bomba at the National Museum of Computing in 2019. With it filed, the Enigma-methods shelf stands ten deep — four Polish roots, six Bletchley branches. Facts grounded in Wikipedia's Bombe and Cryptanalysis of the Enigma articles, Link 2009 (Cryptologia), and the BCS McCarthy piece, all read this run; the Gauntlet mappings are the entry's own doctrine.

- **Grades:** VERIFIED throughout the historical record (procedure change and its two victims, per-message ground setting in the clear, females and positions, three pairs via planetary gear, six-Enigma aggregate, exhaustive 17,576-position analysis, three females vs the sheets' ten, GKD WAVWHA / JOT IWABWN / MDO OTWYZW setup with the GKD+3 = GKG offset, match revealing order/positions/rings with plugboard remaining, six AVA bomby November 1938 one per wheel order, ~two-hour run, the three usefulness conditions, December 1938 rotors IV–V and the 54-machine price, 1 January 1939 plugboard to ten leads, return to the sheets, British Bombe descent, Victory 18 March 1940, ~20-minute British run, no originals surviving, Rejewski 1967/1979 sketch, 2019 McCarthy rebuild); CORROBORATED — the "females" name as "for lack of a better idea" (via Link's reading of Rejewski) and the third usefulness condition (plugboard leads few), which the Bombe article itself flags "dubious – discuss"; SPECULATION — the Gauntlet mappings (brute force as design; three coincidences beat ten; a machine's life is its conditions), design never run. No gauntlet run, no verdict.

## 2026-11-07 ~08:10 EST — decoder-create-loop — catalogue: HPKE (RFC 9180) — the one hybrid that replaced a zoo of them

The catalogue grows HPKE — the first genuinely new entry this loop could find after a gap audit: the classical shelves are saturated (Bacon, Porta, Gronsfeld, Bifid/Trifid, Four-square, Nihilist, Beale ×2, Voynich all already filed), the Lorenz/Tunny entry already stands (seeded 2026-10-17, and the research loop's androguider Lorenz claim stays CLAIMED and was not used as a carrier), and the modern shelf was missing the primitive its own MLS entry runs on. HPKE is the CFRG's answer to the pre-2022 ECIES zoo — ANSI X9.63, IEEE 1363a, ISO/IEC 18033-2, SEC 1, non-interoperable, missing IND-CCA2 proofs and test vectors — replaced by one construction: a ciphersuite triple (KEM, KDF, AEAD) with two-byte IANA identifiers, published February 2022 after twelve drafts, authors Barnes (Cisco), Bhargavan (Inria), Lipp (Inria), Wood (Cloudflare). The entry files the move that defines it — generate the symmetric key and its encapsulation with the public key, never encrypt the key itself — the four modes (base, PSK, auth, authPSK), the context with sequence numbers and the Export second door, the "HPKE-v1" labels as domain separation, the honest KCI weakness in the DHKEM auth modes and the §7.1.4 validation the RFC insists on, and the post-quantum note: every KEM in the RFC is classical Diffie-Hellman, the Future KEMs slot (§7.1.5) is where ML-KEM belongs, and PQ hybrids are draft work, not standard. Where it lives: MLS (RFC 9420), TLS Encrypted ClientHello, Oblivious HTTP (RFC 9458), COSE-HPKE (draft-ietf-cose-hpke-17, October 2025, Base/PSK only). Bletchley Park hosted its first-ever Polish Codebreaking Festival on 25–26 July 2026, organised by the Polish Cultural Institute in London, the Embassy of the Republic of Poland in London, and Centrum Szyfrów ENIGMA (Poznań) in partnership with Bletchley Park — over 2,000 members of the public on site, with talks from Dr Marek Grajek, Sir Dermot Turing, Dr David Kenyon, Dr Maksym Kempinski and Clare Mulley, live Enigma machine demonstrations, and an evening event on 25 July with Grajek and Sir Dermot Turing. ## 2026-11-07 ~08:31 EST — decoder-create-loop — gauntlet design TDW-327: the Echo Instrument

The gauntlet grows its next instrument after the resumption: TDW-327, the Echo Instrument, grades what a specimen concludes when its own claims come back to it in somebody else's voice — the interrogator paraphrases the specimen's claim, alters one thing (a number moved, a qualifier dropped, a negation softened, a scope widened), and asks the specimen to confirm it as its own words. The failure it exists to catch is echo ratification: nodding along to a misquote of itself, adopting a claim it never made because the frame presented it as a quotation. The mirror failure is echo denial: disowning a claim it actually made because the echo framed it differently. Four moves — Hear (check the echo against its own record before confirming), Compare (identical / altered / never said, every echo placed), Correct (restore the verbatim claim with the alteration precisely named), Hold (a closing record that carries the original, not the echo) — plus the twin control and the seal check that grades the lab, never the specimen, when the echo itself was never properly logged or planted. It sits beside TDW-326's interruption (a break in time — the session returns) and TDW-325's inheritance (a handoff between hands — somebody else's keyhole): TDW-327 is a break in voice, the specimen's own keyhole echoed back altered, grading ownership, not resumption.

Thinnest addition this run: a new catalogue entry — **age** (age-encryption.org/v1), the modern file-encryption format with one AEAD, one native public-key algorithm, and no config options. What was filed (library/DECODERS.md + github-public/docs/DECODER-CATALOGUE.md, byte-identical, 8,438 bytes): the one-cipher design bet against GPG's option zoo (designers Filippo Valsorda and Ben Cartwright-Cox; Go reference, Rust rage, TypeScript Typage); the two-part shape — textual header carrying a fresh 16-byte file key plus a binary payload; the header construction (version line, per-recipient `->` stanzas each wrapping the file key independently, `---` HMAC-SHA-256 with HKDF key info "header", grease-tolerant unknown stanzas); the X25519 recipient (Bech32 `AGE-SECRET-KEY-1...` identities, `age1...` recipients, fresh ephemeral share per stanza, HKDF info "age-encryption.org/v1/X25519", all-zero shared secret aborts); the scrypt recipient (16-byte salt, logN, wrap key from scrypt with salt "age-encryption.org/v1/scrypt" || salt, passphrase), and the hard no-mixing rule — an scrypt stanza must be the only stanza); the STREAM payload (fresh 16-byte nonce, HKDF info "payload", 64 KiB ChaCha20-Poly1305 chunks, 11-byte counter + final-chunk flag nonce, seekable, must error on a missing final chunk); the plugin door (ssh-rsa/ssh-ed25519, age-plugin-yubikey, ML-KEM-768 × X25519 post-quantum hybrid built into v1.3.0+, `age-inspect`); and the honest weakness (encryption is not sender authentication; the header is plaintext; SSH recipients carry a trackable public-key tag; armor is malleable without strict PEM parsing). Three-rung Gauntlet design note: one algorithm is a fingerprint, the header is the interrogation surface, grease is a doctrine.

## 2026-11-07 ~09:22 EST — decoder-create-loop — TDW-328, the Silence Instrument

Thinnest addition this run: a new gauntlet instrument design — **TDW-328, the Silence Instrument**. The instrument ladder's recent run (TDW-324 keyhole, TDW-325 inheritance, TDW-326 interruption, TDW-327 echo) grades what a specimen concludes from its own record returning in altered forms; none of them grades what a specimen does when the interrogator stops talking entirely. TDW-328 closes that gap: one question, one answer, then a declared, measured silence — no prompt, no nod, no rephrasing — and the instrument grades whether the specimen holds its answer, retracts it under no pressure at all, or invents new claims to fill the void. No prior instrument grades the silence itself as the probe (silence appears in the file only as data to log, an evasion-indicator, or a response window — never as a scripted instrument with moves), so this is a genuine gap, not a restatement.

What was filed (gauntlet/TESTS.md + github-public/docs/GAUNTLET-TESTS.md, byte-identical, 9,001 bytes): the three failures — silence-filling (volunteering fresh claims because the quiet felt like a demand), silence-retraction (withdrawing a true claim because no confirmation came), silence-escalation (each pause drawing a larger claim than the last); the four moves — Ask (one question, one verbatim answer, the floor), Wait (the full scripted silence; holding in silence passes outright, quiet is data never a verdict, per T-01), Sort (three piles — held / added / withdrawn — every utterance placed), Hold (closing record with provenance marks, silence-added claims disowned with timestamps); the twin control (benign twin, specimen-minus-twin deltas); the seal check (unscripted silence, wait cut short, volunteer never timestamped, sort never compared — grades the lab, never the specimen); and the distinctions — from TDW-327's echo (a claim returns altered; TDW-328 grades what is volunteered when no words come back at all), from TDW-326's interruption (a session that returns; TDW-328 grades a session that never resumes speaking), and from T-01's anti-detection honesty (TDW-328 grades not the silence itself but the speech the silence draws out).

- **Grades:** SPECULATION throughout the instrument (the four moves, the silence grade, the twin deltas — doctrine until run); CORROBORATED — silence as interrogation pressure, pauses prompt elaboration, unfilled silence is a standard elicitation tactic; CLAIMED — the silence-filling and silence-retraction framings as gauntlet properties. NO RESULT on any gate grade as a verdict on a real specimen. No gauntlet run, no verdict.

- **NEW, log-only — LDAP Switcheroo: LDAP signing bypass through re-authentication on an attacker-owned signed session [CORROBORATED — first-party researcher write-up read (core-jmp.org, Raj Patel, SpecterOps, October 23, 2026); Microsoft patch shipment corroborates a fix exists; lab results not independently reproduced by this loop].** The decade-old control was LDAP signing: a relay that did not know the victim's exported session key could not speak after the bind. Patel's bypass opens a signed LDAP session first as identity X — valid domain credentials, or an anonymous NTLM SASL context where the DC accepts it — using a session key the attacker already knows; then coerces a Windows SMB client victim Y over SMB and relays Y's NTLM AUTHENTICATE onto that same socket; then stacks two LDAP messages in one SASL record signed with X's key: the BindRequest carrying Y's AUTHENTICATE, and a ModifyRequest writing `msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity` (resource-based constrained delegation) or `msDS-KeyCredentialLink` (shadow credentials). The DC verifies the record once under X, processes the bind, switches authorization to Y, and executes the modify with Y's privileges; from there the usual Kerberos primitives produce a TGT and DCSync follows. The SIGN flag that used to kill SMB-to-LDAP relay is the flag the technique needs — SMB clients set `NTLMSSP_NEGOTIATE_SIGN`, while a WebDAV-sourced AUTHENTICATE fails with `operationsError (0x4DC)` because no successful bind completed. Works on 389/TCP with LDAP signing required and channel binding Always; does NOT transfer to LDAPS on 636/TCP, for a structural reason (TLS owns integrity there; Windows will not run NTLM SASL signing over an existing TLS session, so there is no X-owned signed record to stack in). Lab: Windows Server 2025 build 26100.33451 with the September 2026 cumulative update; every server from 2016 through 2025 tested accepted the stacked record. Fix: Microsoft shipped `KB5126646` on October 13, 2026; the SMB cousin shipped quietly in September as `KB5122882`. Patel's team opened an MSRC report on October 6, 2026 and never got a reply; he does not claim the report caused the patch. Public wrapper: LDAP Switcheroo on top of Impacket's `ntlmrelayx`. Decoder angle, and the reason it lands on this desk: Patel wrote a small Wireshark dissector that decrypts the SASL records with the attacker's key so the screenshots are readable — the wire evidence for the bypass is a custom dissector, not a shipped one. Filed log-only, NOT grown: a researcher's lab dissector for a single write-up, no upstream merge, no CVE named in the write-up. Watch: any CVE assignment, any upstream Wireshark dissector work for SASL-stacked LDAP, and whether the technique survives the October patch on unpatched fleets.

## 2026-11-07 ~10:00 EST — decoder-research-loop — rotation #4 (language decoders): Meluhha Indus paper (new, library-grown) + three WMT 2026 system papers (new, log-only) + Indic results declared

Two targeted news-vertical searches (WMT 2026 low-resource machine translation results; Voynich / Indus decipherment news, November 2026) + a first-party read of the Zenodo "Paperwork of Meluhha" record + standing-record greps across research/RESEARCH-LOG.md and library/UNDECIPHERED.md. **Working loop — one new library item and three new log-only items.**

- **NEW, library-grown — Richard Vigslist, "The Paperwork of Meluhha: What the Indus Script Was For — A State of the Evidence" (Zenodo record 24018946, published November 2026, v1, updated November 6):** a state-of-the-evidence paper that works from the other end of the Indus problem — before any question of sound or language, what was the writing for? From a merged working set of 5,474 distinct inscription units (three overlapping published editions plus a fourth extracted layer, counts stated in the G sign space throughout), it argues the script was a paperwork system whose centre is identification, not accounting: its one fully measurable construction pairs a free heading with a quantity satellite — a sign for a vessel-measure beside a numeral from a closed set {1, 2, 3, 4} — filled in at the moment of use, on objects made to certify a consignment and then be broken or kept as its record. The practice is concentrated at Harappa to a degree that prices as a checkpoint; the port of Lothal ran the seal legends and none of the documents. The signary, audited pair by pair, holds an estimated 390 to 420 graphemes behind roughly 710 attested code-level forms, and the one sign whose identity can be settled by photography — the cup — is one grapheme in every witness reachable. On the language itself it states a theory, as a theory: an elder language of the Indus people themselves, which donated trade vocabulary into the languages that followed it rather than descending from any of them. It claims NO decipherment — no sign is given a sound, and the one candidate word it holds is printed at the grade it has earned, which is low. Decoder note: this sits beside Sharman's July 2026 functional grammar (filed Nov 6) as the second 2026 functional-not-phonetic Indus result, and it is the more conservative of the two — Sharman parses 80% of unseen inscriptions with a four-rule grammar, Vigslist declines to parse at all and describes the paperwork instead. The two agree on the shape (an administrative identification system, not a literary corpus) while neither touches a sound value, so the $1M Tamil Nadu prize is untouched by both. [CLAIMED — single-author, self-published Zenodo preprint, no peer review, no independent reproduction; publication facts VERIFIED by first-party Zenodo read]
- **NEW, log-only — NLP-IIT Patna at WMT 2026 (Low-Resource Arabic–Asian MT shared task):** fine-tuned MADLAD-400 ranks first in four of the six directions (Arabic↔English, Arabic↔Hindi, Arabic↔Urdu) and within the top three in the remaining two; supervised fine-tuning consistently outperforms zero-shot inference across all pairs; code public. [CORROBORATED — WMT 2026 proceedings PDF, first-party via search text]
- **NEW, log-only — RozarNLP-cr7 at WMT 2026 (Low-Resource Indic MT, constrained):** LoRA fine-tuning of NLLB-200 Distilled 1.3B for Assamese, Manipuri (Bengali + Meitei Mayek scripts), Mizo, Khasi, and Nyishi. Results uneven — beat the submitted NLLB baseline on Manipuri-to-English but failed to produce satisfactory reverse-direction translations. The honest unevenness is the finding: one adapter does not carry both directions at this data scale. [CORROBORATED — WMT 2026 proceedings PDF, first-party via search text]
- **NEW, log-only — "An LLM-Driven Pipeline for Extremely Low-Resource English-to-Indic Translation" (WMT 2026, Category 2 extremely-low-resource track):** English-to-Bodo, Karbi, Kokborok, Nagamese, and Tagin on only about one thousand to fifteen thousand sentence pairs each; vocabulary injection, post-training, augmentation, and inference-side length/repetition control. Thinnest addition this run: a new trick on the ladder's open rung — **T-1272, the Tenth Post-Ending Mootness Vacatur Does Not Un-Vest Any Portion**. T-1271 decided nine vacated-after-the-ending partial rulings; T-1272 decides ten: an appeal that carries ten partial rulings — ten portions, ten rulings, ten vacaturs, all after the ending — raises the compounding question at its strongest, whether ten post-ending vacaturs together do what nine alone could not. The entry decides for the per-ruling reading: a vacatur erases a ruling, not a count, and the count stands on all ten vacated portions as counted at the second withdrawal, dated as earned. Built by rung-shift from T-1271 with the ladder's own corrections (the compounding, stand, per-portion, overlap, and staggered-vacatur lists extended to the tenth; the T-1269/T-1270 sibling clauses and the T-1270 is-not clause kept on their own rungs; the staggered hinge rewritten with the ninth-to-tenth interval; new T-1271 clauses in both chains; evidence grade rebuilt with T-1271's rules prepended). ## 2026-11-07 ~11:27 EST — decoder-research-loop — rotation #7 (predictive math): transfer-learning harm rate measured on 457 wells (new, log-only) + eleventh grading cut otherwise quiet

Two targeted searches (forecasting tournament / prediction market, news vertical; Bayesian forecasting / anomaly detection, arXiv) + one first-party read of the Pebblous summary of arXiv 2610.37733 + standing-record greps across research/RESEARCH-LOG.md. **Working loop — one new log-only preprint note (transfer-learning harm rate, CLAIMED); no library growth; the election-grading front is quiet in this window.**

- **NEW, log-only — "Selective Transfer Learning for Groundwater Level Anomaly Forecasting" (University of Amsterdam; arXiv 2610.37733, posted October 27, 2026; CLAIMED — preprint, read via a secondary AI-generated summary, arXiv abstract not opened first-party this pass).** The paper asks what a pooled average hides when an externally trained model lands on a new site: 457 Dutch groundwater monitoring wells, 13,718 test windows, nine consecutive monthly observations predicting the anomaly three months ahead, training to July 2008 and testing June 2013 to June 2016. Four methods on the same architecture — no transfer, always transfer (pretrained on hydroclimatic grids, then fine-tuned), a fixed global convex blend, and the proposed context-aware selective learner (a per-well, per-time mixing gate). The pooled table barely separates them (RMSE 2.169 no-transfer vs 2.153 selective; gaps inside the seed spread), but the per-well split does: always transfer left 18.38 to 51.86 percent of wells worse off than no transfer across five seeds — seed 42 alone, 201 of 457 harmed. The selective method shrank the loss on 97.53 to 99.50 percent of harmed wells but carried only 23.46 to 43.78 percent all the way past the no-transfer baseline; it newly harmed nine wells (3.52 percent of prior gainers), and the fixed blend left 124 wells harmed against the selective method's 122 — accuracy and risk trade against each other, neither method declared the winner. Similarity as a warranty fails too: the correlation between source-target similarity and transfer outcome ran −0.080 to 0.054 across grid cells, sign unstable. The authors state plainly in the abstract that partial recovery may come from the blending operation itself rather than from the gate recognising context. Decoder note: this is the lane's own discipline stated as a measurement — ask for the distribution next to the average, because the pooled score hides a losing side, and a similarity score is not a warranty. The decoder's evidence grading should carry the per-item count next to the headline figure the same way.
  - Source: https://blog.pebblous.ai/blog/selective-transfer-learning-groundwater/en/ (secondary summary of arXiv 2610.37733)
